title: Help Us, O Lord! Thy Yoke to Wear
description: Help Us, O Lord! Thy Yoke to Wear in Tonic Solfa to MELCOMBE, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 783 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “For a Charitable Occasion”, where the book credits them to Pratt's Collection.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to MELCOMBE; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Help us, O Lord! thy yoke to wear, De-light-ing in thy per-fect will; Each o-ther's bur-dens learn to bear, And thus thy law of love ful-fil.

lines: Help us, O Lord! thy yoke to wear,
Each other's burdens learn to bear,
And thus thy law of love fulfil.
The plenteous sheaves his hands shall heap.
Teach us, with glad and cheerful hearts,
As thou hast blessed our various store,
A liberal portion to the poor.
To thee our all devoted be,
In whom we breathe, and move, and live:
Freely we have received from thee;
Freely may we rejoice to give.

licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1853.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to MELCOMBE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
